messages:
releasebot: Planned toggle: enable `llm-routing-alpha` to 10% for cohort `alpha-3` at 2026-03-21T22:00Z (night window). Ramp plan: 10% -> 30% after 30m -> 70% after 2h if health gates pass. Exclude EU and APAC regions for initial rollout. Pin traffic to model v3.0.0-alpha. Please ack and call out telemetry or runway concerns.
harper: ack. will watch token-cost and per-request cpu. adding cost dashboard: https://graf.redwood.company/d/costs/llm-night-canary
julia: quick ask: add a temporary token-length cap (max_tokens=1024) for canary to limit tail-cost spikes. can we do that in the flag metadata?
releasebot: yes, flag metadata supports overrides. adding max_tokens cap to canary manifest.
deploybot: note: deploybot will set auto-hold if "cost_per_1000_tokens" > baseline by 30% for 10m OR if error rate > 2% absolute. Manual resume required after auto-hold.
infra-bot: FYI - housekeeping: route-service will pin resolver to commit `3a1f9e` during canary. logs will be streamed to s3://redwood-logs/canary/alpha-3/
ops-bot: Prom rule: `llm_inference_error_rate` currently 0.7% baseline. watching for >2% absolute.
harper: also suggest adding a short-circuit for long-running requests (>6s) to fail-fast and not build KV pressure.
julia: good call. added fail-fast to canary config.
releasebot: updated release notes draft: "Night window canary for routing alpha; model pinned to v3.0.0-alpha; token cap 1024; fail-fast 6s; regional exclusions: EU/APAC." Please review.
harper: lgtm.
deploybot: initiating toggle -> 10% for alpha-3 now. action_id:6580001120
ops-bot: probe: synthetic journey (user: synth-night-02) returned in 1.2s at 22:01Z.
ops-bot: alert: cost-per-1000_tokens increased +34% in canary at 22:03Z (sampled).
releasebot: auto-hold condition hit (cost >30% for 3m). deploybot: pausing ramp and holding at 10%. tagging @oncall.
oncall: acknowledged. pulling recent traces and flamegraphs.
harper: rolling back token cap? that seems odd since we added cap; maybe higher-cost model path triggered.
julia: can you dump a sample of high-cost requests? small sample with request ids please.
infra-bot: logs: s3://redwood-logs/canary/alpha-3/sample_high_cost_ids.txt (contains 12 ids).
deploybot: temp mitigation options: 1) scale canary workers + cache priming 2) revert flag to 0% 3) enforce stricter token cap (512) and retry. Recommend 3) then re-evaluate.
harper: prefer 3) + cache priming. do 512 cap and run quick prefix priming job.
releasebot: prepping update: set max_tokens=512 for cohort alpha-3; apply cache-priming job to top 1K prefixes; keep hold until metrics stable for 10m.
ops-bot: running priming job now. progress: 60% completed.
oncall: running trace triage: a small fraction of requests hit expensive rerank path — possibly from new model policy. flag metadata shows rerank_enabled=true for alpha-3.
julia: oh — rerank_enabled was mistakenly turned on in canary manifest. that explains cost. can we flip rerank_enabled=false for canary?
releasebot: updating manifest: rerank_enabled=false, max_tokens=512. applying now.
deploybot: update applied at 22:09Z (action_id:6580001150).
ops-bot: priming job completed at 22:10Z. synthetic check pass.
harper: monitoring metrics. please post p95 and cost delta samples.
ops-bot: p95 back to baseline (1.03x) at 22:12Z. cost delta down to +8% at 22:13Z.
oncall: recommend holding 20 more minutes before resuming ramp given signal recovery.
julia: agree. also please note we should update release notes to mention rerank toggle mistake and mitigation.
releasebot: updated release notes and added incident tag for follow-up. plan: keep alpha-3 at 10% for 30m post-recovery, then move to 30% if stable. thread open until ramp continues or revert. :white_check_mark:
